comparisons.peer_summary: The firm may modify terms for borrowers in financial difficulty, primarily via term extensions; modified loans were mostly performing, with negligible defaults in 2024 and ~$100 million charged off in 2023 from previously modified loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS disclose the volume and nature of loan modifications for borrowers in financial difficulty, but they differ significantly in reported volume and specific financial impact metrics. BAC reports $650 million in modified credit card and consumer loans in 2024, highlighting a 18.89% weighted-average interest rate reduction and $113 million in principal forgiveness. In contrast, GS states that modifications were primarily term extensions (increasing term by 19 months) and does not disclose specific volume totals or principal forgiveness amounts in the same sentence structure, noting instead that modified loans represented ~2% of corporate and ~1% of CRE and credit card loans. GS also highlights that defaults on modified loans were not material in 2024, whereas BAC focuses on the immediate financial relief (rate reduction/forgiveness) rather than default rates in the primary volume disclosure.

sentences.text: The December 31, 2024 amortized cost of credit card and other consumer loans that were modified through these programs during 2024 was $650 million compared to $598 million in 2023.

During 2024, the financial effect of modifications resulted in a weighted-average interest rate reduction of 18.89 percent compared to 19.02 percent in 2023, and principal forgiveness of $113 million compared to $61 million in 2023.

• Loan modifications during both 2024 and 2023 were primarily in the form of term extensions. These extensions increased the weighted average term by 19 months for loans modified during 2024 and by 16 months for loans modified during 2023.

• Substantially all of the modified loans were related to corporate loans, commercial real estate loans and credit cards. Modified loans represented approximately 2% of corporate loans (at amortized cost), and approximately 1% of both commercial real estate loans (at amortized cost) and credit card loans (at amortized cost).

• During 2024, loans that defaulted after being modified were not material. During 2023, the firm charged off approximately $100 million of loans that had defaulted after being modified. Substantially all of the remaining modified loans were performing in accordance with the modified contractual terms as of both December 2024 and December 2023.

comparisons.peer_topic: Financial effects of loan modifications for the year ended December 31, 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: For the year ended December 31, 2024, retained residential real estate financial distress modifications (FDMs) totaled $206 million. These modifications, predominantly term extensions and interest rate reductions, extended the weighted-average loan life by 15 years and reduced the weighted-average contractual interest rate from 7.53% to 5.44%.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose the financial effects of loan modifications, specifically interest rate reductions, but for different loan portfolios and with different magnitudes. BAC reports on 'credit card and other consumer' loans, noting a $650 million modification volume with an average rate reduction of 18.89%. JPM reports on 'retained residential real estate' FDMs, which totaled $206 million, with a rate reduction from 7.53% to 5.44% (a roughly 2.09 percentage point drop) and a significant extension of loan life by 15 years. While both involve rate reductions for distressed borrowers, BAC's modifications include principal forgiveness ($113 million) not mentioned by JPM, and JPM emphasizes term extension more heavily than BAC in this specific comparison.

sentences.text: The December 31, 2024 amortized cost of credit card and other consumer loans that were modified through these programs during 2024 was $650 million compared to $598 million in 2023.

During 2024, the financial effect of modifications resulted in a weighted-average interest rate reduction of 18.89 percent compared to 19.02 percent in 2023, and principal forgiveness of $113 million compared to $61 million in 2023.
For the year ended December 31, 2024, retained residential real estate FDMs were $206 million.

The financial effects of the FDMs, which were predominantly in the form of term extensions and interest rate reductions, included extending the weighted-average life of the loans by 15 years, and reducing the weighted-average contractual interest rate from 7.53% to 5.44% for the year ended December 31, 2024.
